summary.intent: Land typed checker-request refactor (#521) and address a review finding on change #316/#518, where package_of repeatedly walks ancestor directories on every call.
summary.outcome: #521 (refactor/typed-checker-requests, trail 470) was reviewed, found merge-clean with #519, and its PR body published. A worker was dispatched on the #518 branch to add a per-directory package result cache beside the probe cache, with a test and re-measurement; the fix had not landed yet.

repo: Typed checker requests: `Ask` enum (one variant per checker method, generated from a single `asks!` list) replaces untagged `Asking`; `Rpc::call` takes a typed `Request`, and session-level params (initialize, createSnapshot, updateSnapshot, release, batchRequests) are structs.
`checker.rs` and `on_demand.rs` still build some raw requests with `json!` outside the `Rpc` layer, so the typed guarantee covers only requests sent through `Rpc`.
Exact request counts on Mantine and antd vary between main's own runs, so they cannot be used as an identity check; three in-repo fixtures are identical instead.
Verification lanes used: `just lint doc-check machete typos`, workspace nextest (1732 passed), `just test-checker-lane`; output-identity checked against origin/main on Mantine and antd.

code.finding: `package_of` now walks every ancestor directory on each call, doing a map lookup and `Arc` clone per ancestor; base did one map lookup after the first walk. Likely cause of the ~0.6% extra instructions on Mantine.
`learn` calls `package_of` for each uncached export lookup, so repeated same-directory lookups multiply the ancestor-walk cost.
Writing the index repeats the `package_of` lookup for each export row.

workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output, not user approval; review the branch and evidence independently before publishing.
Do a dry-run merge against other open PRs (e.g. #519) before declaring a PR ready.
Fixes for review findings should include a test that fails on the current head, mutation proof, and before/after instruction/CPU measurements.

friction: Mantine/antd request counts are nondeterministic on main, preventing exact request-count comparison.
Corpus runs for #521 were on ffaa9465, before the heap-check follow-up.
#518 has accumulated four review findings for only ~1-11% fewer filesystem calls and no wall-time/CPU gain.
open_items: Wait for the worker's package_of result-cache fix on #518, then resolve the finding on Entire with the commit and test.
Decide on #518: assistant recommends closing it and splitting out the test-only differential test.
#519 (readonly from flags) and #521 are ready for the user's review.
Docs PR for the performance record is pending.
Next candidate: the timeout-as-loud-watchdog item (rpc.rs now settled in #521), or the #518 split.
Remaining raw `json!` requests in `checker.rs` and `on_demand.rs` could be typed later.
